question: What visual acuity score is used to define legal blindness in the better eye?
explanation: Legal blindness is defined as a best-corrected visual acuity of 20/200 or worse in the better eye. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h1)

question: How is low vision different from total blindness?

options.A: Total absence of light perception and eye movement
options.B: Temporary blurriness that responds to eye drops
options.C: Some remaining usable sight despite using glasses
options.D: Completely normal vision in one eye only

explanation: Low vision means a person still has some functional sight left, even though standard glasses cannot fully correct it. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h1)

question: Which eye condition involves the clouding of the natural lens?
explanation: Cataracts happen when proteins break down and cloud the lens, blocking light from reaching the retina. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h2)

question: Glaucoma mainly damages which part of the eye to cause vision loss?
explanation: High pressure inside the eye puts stress on the optic nerve, leading to a gradual loss of side vision. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h2)

question: What term describes the complete inability to see any light at all?
explanation: Total blindness means there is an absolute loss of sight where the patient cannot perceive light. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h3)

question: A patient with tunnel vision can still see straight ahead, but what part of their vision is severely restricted?
explanation: Tunnel vision narrows a person's outer or side vision while often leaving their central vision clear. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h3)

question: What is the best first step when walking into a room to care for a patient with poor vision?

options.A: Turn off the overhead lights to protect their eyes
options.B: Touch their shoulder gently to wake them up
options.C: Announce your name and presence clearly
options.D: Stand quietly at the bedside until they notice you

explanation: Speaking up right away prevents startling the patient and builds clear, respectful communication. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h4)

question: When assessing a patient with vision loss, what should the nurse focus on evaluating?
explanation: Checking a sensory deficit helps the nurse figure out how it affects the patient's independence and safety. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h4)

question: Which home modification best helps a visually impaired patient safely navigate a staircase?

options.A: Placing a patterned decorative rug at the top landing
options.B: Applying brightly colored contrasting tape to step edges
options.C: Dimming the hallway lights to reduce eye strain and glare
options.D: Waxing the wooden steps to make them smooth and shiny

explanation: High-contrast visual markers on step edges make depth perception and stair transitions much easier to distinguish. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h5)

question: Why are loose throw rugs dangerous for someone with poor vision?

options.A: They interfere with white canes and walkers
options.B: They absorb too much light and darken the floor
options.C: They easily slip or curl up, causing hard-to-see tripping hazards
options.D: They trap dust that causes eye infections

explanation: Poor vision makes it tough to spot curled rug edges, which greatly increases the risk of a dangerous fall. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h5)

question: What is the main job of a white cane used by someone with vision loss?

options.A: Measuring exact distances to walls and doors
options.B: Detecting obstacles and changes in the ground ahead
options.C: Amplifying sounds to make up for poor vision
options.D: Acting as an antenna for digital GPS trackers

explanation: The white cane works like an extra arm, sweeping the floor to find curbs and steps before the user walks into them. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h6)

question: Which healthcare professional trains visually impaired patients to travel safely?
explanation: Orientation and mobility specialists teach patients how to travel independently and safely indoors and outdoors. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h6)

question: How should a nurse explain where food is on a tray to a patient who cannot see well?

options.A: Point directly to each item while naming them
options.B: Use the clock face method to describe food positions
options.C: Mix all the food together so it is easy to eat
options.D: Feed the patient spoonful by spoonful without talking

explanation: The clock face method gives a clear spatial guide so patients can find and identify their food on their own. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h7)

question: What is the correct way for a nurse to guide a visually impaired patient while walking?

options.A: The patient walks three steps ahead holding a rope
options.B: The patient holds the nurse's elbow and walks slightly behind
options.C: The nurse holds the patient's hand and pulls them forward
options.D: The nurse pushes the patient in a wheelchair for safety

explanation: Having the patient hold the nurse's elbow lets them feel the guide's movements and walking pace naturally. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h7)

question: Why should nurses advise family members not to overprotect a visually impaired patient?

options.A: Overprotection can hurt the patient's independence and self-esteem
options.B: Patients need strict isolation to stop eye infections
options.C: Family members might hurt their backs lifting the patient
options.D: Overprotection makes the patient's eyesight get worse faster

explanation: Doing everything for the patient out of fear can cause learned helplessness and a loss of practical skills. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h8)

question: Which emotional reaction is common in patients who have just been told they have permanent vision loss?

options.A: Grief and mourning over lost independence
options.D: Total indifference with no emotional reaction

explanation: Losing your sight is a major life change that often triggers a normal grieving process similar to other profound losses. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T8#GNS324_U4_T8_h8)
